body.estimand_functional: \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), where \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\) is certified by the face-robust three-coordinate all-count diagonal; equivalently the fixed independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) and the unrestricted design game have the same second-order value at this contrast.

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm.  The face-robust prior is fixed independently of that design; conditioning on an allocation count and unit-permutation invariance reduce every design to the exact finite orbit likelihood without loss.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units with three binary potential outcomes; the exact response-count orbit retains all eight response types.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one of three arm labels is assigned to each unit, and the observation is the assigned label together with its binary outcome.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed.  Positive local counts, positive exterior counts, and zero-count faces are proved separately.  Exact face-guard directions make the target remain uncertain whenever any active arm is unobserved.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation.  Two compact prior coordinates lie in contrast-orthogonal directions: one changes the unequal-arm response geometry and one shifts all arm means together.  Their widths are held fixed in each uniform calculation and then decreased on a computably slow diagonal.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The unrestricted two-arm binary minimax risk equals \(n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and is attained by Bernoulli randomization with nonlinear shrinkage.
For the two-arm bounded-outcome game, independent assignment remains minimax when estimators are unrestricted.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

body.tldr: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the unrestricted outcome-independent design game and the fixed independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) have the same sharp second-order coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\).  The proof replaces the refuted scalar tube by a three-coordinate response-type prior.  Its common-shift coordinate gives exact guards for every single-arm and two-arm allocation face, a derived van Trees envelope controls all positive allocation counts, and the permutation-orbit argument covers arbitrary dependent labeled designs.  A terminating rational evaluator supplies finite lower and upper certificates and a computable tail majorant.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent supplied the first-order value, the second-order order, and finite response-type games, but no sharp all-design coefficient.  A scalar Airy path fails on a zero face because one arm reveals its longitudinal coordinate.  The missing mathematical object was a design-independent full-dimensional local prior together with a uniform finite-population Bayes transfer over local, exterior, and zero-count allocations.
project_justification.niche: At the unequal three-arm contrast, the zero-cost common-mean direction and the nonzero transverse direction jointly hide the target coordinate on every proper allocation face without changing the causal estimand.  This face geometry is absent from the two-arm Airy problem and is essential when designs may put zero probability on an arm.
project_justification.fill: The response alphabet is solved by explicit signed tangent measures.  The resulting compact rational three-coordinate prior has exact positivity and target moments.  A direction-wise van Trees inequality, an exact Horvitz--Thompson covariance identity, and the allocation identity \(H(q)-1=\sum_a(q_a-q_a^\dagger)^2/q_a\) yield a computable uniform Bayes envelope.  Diagonalizing verified rational Airy splines and transverse widths gives the sharp all-design limit, a total attaining procedure, and effective finite-to-limit certificates.

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) and Hull (2026) establish two-arm sharp minimax results.  The present result derives the unequal three-arm coefficient under the larger class of every outcome-independent dependent design.  Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) motivate limit-experiment and spectral methods, but the response-type positivity, realized finite-population target correction, allocation-face guards, exact orbit transfer, and computable uniform remainder are derived here.  Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) impose different estimator, law, or first-order restrictions.  Hammer et al. (1996) supplies only prospective complete binary-endpoint regimen-trial motivation; no censored-outcome reanalysis is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(K=3,n=3\) full-label risk \(511653/4000000\) lies below the scalar Bayes value \(18213/136000\), and the preserved scalar diagnostic explains why that path cannot prove the asymptotic theorem.  The successful prior adds a common-shift guard; its fixed-width face paths are load-bearing.  The theorem is pointwise in the fixed rational contrast and fixed arm count.  It does not provide a computationally uniform modulus as a contrast weight vanishes, and the evaluator's exhaustive finite alphabets are not claimed to run in polynomial time.
body.honest_scope: The unrestricted sharp equality, equality of the independent and unrestricted second-order values, and the cross-sample effective certificate are proved for \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) with fixed three-arm support and binary outcomes.  The response-cost program and fixed-independent theorem remain available for other fixed permitted contrasts, but no unrestricted sharp theorem is claimed there.  No growing-arm, uniform vanishing-weight, censored-endpoint, or arbitrary-real computability claim is made.  Real contrasts have an explicit mathematical response-cost approximation route, while certified execution requires a rational input representation.
body.interpretation: For the fixed unequal three-regimen contrast, allowing dependent assignment or optimizing over all outcome-independent designs gives no second-order advantage over independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\).  A protocol designer can use the total Airy-feedback procedure and can request an exact finite-sample rational risk bracket plus a certified sample-size threshold for a desired second-order tolerance.
